label: EXERCISE_OF_WILL_3, including love of…: An act of willing can seek absent good, love and delight in…
term: exercise of will, including love of possessed good
definition: An act of willing can seek absent good, love and delight in possessed good, or communicate possessed good insofar as possible. Mentioning such an act does not by itself assert that every being with intellectual power is performing a particular seeking act now.
note: Typed episode interface in AppetitePowerExercise: actual seeking requires absent apprehended good; actual love and delight require possessed apprehended good; communication additionally carries a recipient and possibility witness. Apprehension, possession and actual act relations are explicit semantic primitives, whose interpretation remains open. No temporal transition, selected policy, universal production, capacity-to-exercise implication or identification with HasWill is assumed. The idle and possessedLove interpretations test populated apprehension without actual exercise and love without deficient seeking. These are semantic controls, not registered root results or evidence of divine applicability.
